messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 Alert: High 5xx rate from Meridian VPC egress through private NLB (us-east-1). Spike detected at 2024-06-14T03:07Z. PagerDuty: P12345.
raj (oncall): I'm on it, looking at the NLB target health and SGs. Initial guess: target group flapping or conntrack exhaustion.
sabrina (eng-sre): can you paste the healthcheck logs from the NLB? I want to see backend 502/504 pattern.
raj (oncall): quick dump: ```aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg/meridian-privnet``` shows ~20% unhealthy, reason: HTTP 502 from backend-proxy:8080
carla (meridian-sre): Confirming customer observability: our internal app traces show timeouts to Redis proxy around same time. No recent deploys on our side.
raj (oncall): pinging redis team, but can we temporarily shift Meridian traffic to their standby pool? We can update NLB target registration or weight via DNS.
dns-team: We can do weighted DNS failover using Route53 weighted record. Need a TTL change and new weight. Who will execute?
sabrina (eng-sre): ops-runbook-bot, run runbook `privnet-egress-failover` and print steps.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: privnet-egress-failover v1.2
1) Add standby NLB targets: `aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn <standby-tg> --targets Id=ip:10.0.5.10`
2) Update Route53 weighted record: set weight standby=90 primary=10
3) Monitor 5xx rate and latency for 10m
4) If stable, drain old targets
raj (oncall): I'm going to register standby targets and update weights. Carla, please confirm standby pool has capacity.
carla (meridian-sre): Standby pool ready, capacity 3x normal. OK to shift.
raj (oncall): Executing step 1 and 2 now. ```aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg/standby --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d4e5f``` 
raj (oncall): Route53 change submitted (change-id: ZR12345). Set standby weight=95, primary=5, TTL 30s.
dns-team: Change propagated to most resolvers within 45s.
sabrina (eng-sre): >>observability: 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 1.2% within 2 minutes. Latency stable. Good sign.
carla (meridian-sre): Customer impact: partial degradation for ~6 minutes for sticky sessions. No data loss. We're notifying Meridian product lead.
escalation-lead: Good mitigation. Please keep this as incident P1, collect PCAPs and backend logs for RCA. Also prepare customer post-incident summary.
raj (oncall): taking notes for RCA. Will not re-register unhealthy targets until we have backend team analysis. Attaching quick diffs: ```netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l -> 32000``` maybe conntrack/ephemeral port exhaustion on proxy.
sabrina (eng-sre): Action items: 1) run conntrack scrub on proxy nodes 2) collect `ss -tn state` and `dmesg` 3) temp scale proxy pool if needed.
carla (meridian-sre): We'll run a config check on proxy keepalive and client_idle settings.
ops-runbook-bot: Remediation step recommended: `sudo conntrack -F` on affected nodes. Use one node at a time and monitor.
raj (oncall): I'm going to coordinate with on-call infra to schedule conntrack flush on one node. ETA 10m.
dns-team: Keep weighted DNS in place until backend validated for 30m of stability.
carla (meridian-sre): Affected customers: Meridian corp (enterprise tenant), two internal staging clusters saw retries but recovered. No other tenants.
escalation-lead: Please escalate to oncall rotation for next 4 hours and hand off at 1718504800Z if still open.
raj (oncall): Handoff planned. I'll update the incident doc with all commands, timestamps, and links.
sabrina (eng-sre): Thanks all. If conntrack flush doesn't help, we may fallback to a code-level retry/sentinel on the proxy. Keep me looped.
carla (meridian-sre): Customer-facing note drafted, sending to PL for review.
incident-bot: Incident P12345 update: mitigation applied (weighted DNS failover). Monitoring mode. Severity: P1 -> Under observation.
raj (oncall): will update `#incidents` with postmortem stub after final validation.
carla (meridian-sre): Thanks everyone for quick response :raised_hands:
